notes: The two HEIC photos were converted from their original files to WebP for browser display.
The shared folder contained no subfolders.

Two downloaded clips remain in assets/originals/videos because their project association is unclear. The second same-named 675 KB clip was downloaded and SHA-256 checked, then deduplicated. The 523.8 MB Break the Loop original remains available through its existing Drive link instead of being bundled into the site.
Photography is presented in its own responsive gallery, separate from video projects.
The older Kendrick Lamar link was verified against the matching Drive video title and is retained in the film showcase.
The older Batman link resolves to a Bhasha Utsav video and is not presented as Batman.
The Gokarna Drive link resolves to a video file titled draft 3.mp4; its Gokarna association is retained from the existing portfolio record.
Typographic SVG artwork is used as a fallback poster for each film; none is represented as footage or a frame from the video.

Three additional user-uploaded photographs are preserved in assets/originals/uploads. The city and seaside photos are separate crops from the supplied collage; all three are optimized WebP files used in the Photography gallery.
The three resume-derived decorative photo copies were removed from public/images/decorative so the matching uploaded photographs appear only in the Photography gallery.
The two HEIC originals are decoded at their original pixel dimensions and stored as lossless PNG display sources for browser compatibility.
The city and seaside display crops were re-extracted losslessly from the uploaded collage; the pink blossoms image was re-cropped from its supplied PNG to remove only its outer presentation frame.
The Photography gallery and lightbox now use the local full-resolution source files directly; the former WebP derivatives are retained but are not selected by browser srcset.
The three uploaded photographs remain at the maximum detail in the supplied files; the smaller city, seaside, and blossoms sources are not enlarged beyond their source pixel widths in the gallery.
